title: Clarify for "create a classic/module script" that JavaScript string = ES source text
body:
Right now, the spec says:

> To [**create a classic script**](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#creating-a-classic-script), given a [JavaScript string](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-string) _source_, …
>
> 9. Let _result_ be [ParseScript](https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#sec-parse-script)(_source_, _settings_'s [Realm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#environment-settings-object's-realm), _script_).

> To [**create a JavaScript module script**](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#creating-a-javascript-module-script), given a [JavaScript string](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-string) _source_, …
>
> 7. Let _result_ be [ParseModule](https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#sec-parsemodule)(_source_, _settings_'s [Realm](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#environment-settings-object's-realm), _script_).

> To [**create a JSON module script**](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/webappapis.html#creating-a-json-module-script), given a string _source_…
>
> 5. Let _json_ be ? [Call](https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#sec-call)([%JSONParse%](https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#sec-json.parse), undefined, « _source_ »).

The first two explicitly say that _source_ is a JavaScript string, while the last one just says [string](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#string), which could be taken to mean either JavaScript or scalar value string. But in fact, the first two pass the source to JavaScript abstract operations that take [ECMAScript source text](https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#sec-source-text), which "is a sequence of code points … including surrogate code points." While JavaScript makes a distinction between String and source text, [Infra](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#javascript-string) explicitly says

> A JavaScript string can also be interpreted as containing code points, per the conversion defined in [The String Type](https://tc39.github.io/ecma262/#sec-ecmascript-language-types-string-type) section of the JavaScript specification.
>
> Note: This conversion process converts surrogate pairs into their corresponding scalar value and maps isolated surrogates to their corresponding code point, leaving them effectively as-is.

so it might be good to add a note that we are not actually ignoring the distinction, but they are the same thing in Infra.

"Create a JSON module script" passes _source_ to a JavaScript function, which expects a JavaScript string. It might be good to explicitly say "JavaScript string" also, for consistency and avoidance of confusion.

So two action items:
- Write a note for "create a classic script" and "create a JavaScript module script" that in HTML, JavaScript string = ES String = ES source text.
- Clarify that the "string" "create a JSON module script" takes is in fact a JavaScript string.
